name: Plitvice Lakes, Croatia
note: Water flows between a chain of lakes over natural travertine barriers. The landscape changes as water deposits and dissolves the rock.

name: Meteora, Greece
note: Monasteries stand on immense sandstone pillars above the Thessalian plain, joining a striking natural landscape with centuries of monastic history.

name: Socotra Archipelago, Yemen
note: Long isolation helped this archipelago develop remarkable endemic plants, including the dragon's blood tree.

name: Wadi Rum, Jordan
note: Sandstone mountains, narrow gorges and natural arches rise from the desert. Rock inscriptions record a long history of people moving through this landscape.

name: Yakushima, Japan
note: A mountainous island supports ancient Japanese cedar forests and a remarkable transition of vegetation from coast to high peaks.

name: Iguazú National Park, Argentina
note: A vast system of waterfalls cuts across a forested basalt escarpment. The falls and surrounding subtropical forest form a protected World Heritage landscape.

name: Göreme, Türkiye
note: Erosion shaped volcanic rock into pillars and valleys. Rock-cut sanctuaries and settlements reveal how people made homes within the landscape.

name: Tikal, Guatemala
note: Maya temples rise above tropical forest in a national park that protects both archaeological heritage and a diverse living ecosystem.

name: Kakadu, Australia
note: Wetlands, escarpments and rock art preserve a landscape with a deep and continuing Aboriginal cultural history.

name: Yellowstone, USA
note: Geysers, hot springs and wildlife share a volcanic landscape. Old Faithful can be explored through the park's official webcam pages when available.

name: Brooks River, Katmai, USA
note: Salmon runs draw brown bears to the Brooks River. Public wildlife cameras are seasonal; a camera link does not guarantee bears or a working stream.

name: Yosemite Valley, USA
note: Glacially carved cliffs frame meadows, forest and waterfalls. The national park publishes webcam views of parts of the landscape.
